messages:
Maya: Quick q about handoff semantics between CPU staging pool and GPU allocator. We've seen two flaky OOMs when pages are in-flight during eviction; need a clear ownership contract. Details below.

Chris: Can you list the exact failure modes? Is it double-free, leak, or stale pointer?

Maya: Mostly stale pointer -> use-after-evict: worker holds a vram addr, eviction removes mapping and remote pages get swapped, later worker writes to freed mapping. Also contention when reclaim races with promotion. Example timeline: allocate -> map -> schedule bulk infer -> evict while KV still referenced -> worker resumes and hits bad mapping.

Devin: Great. I think we should consider a lease token model instead of refcounts: holder gets a short-lived lease, evictor revokes/blocks until lease expires. Simpler to reason about across threads/processes. :thinking:

Liam: Lease model sounds good but adds latency on thrash. Can we have two tiers: fast optimistic snapshot + fallback to revoke path? Also need metrics: number of revokes, revoke latency, blocked requests.

Sophia: Proto API suggestion:
```c
// caller gets a lease; must call release()
Lease acquire_page_lease(PageID pid, uint32_t ttl_ms);
bool release_page_lease(Lease l);
// evict path
bool try_evict(PageID pid);
void revoke_lease(Lease l);
```
Revocation is async; evictor waits for TTL or for forced revoke which blocks until release or preempt.

Chris: Edge cases: what about cross-node migration (RDMA)? Lease needs to be cluster-global. TTL must be adjustable and we need fast path for trusted internal threads. Also how do we handle partial ownership (shared read vs exclusive write)?

Maya: Also need to handle fragmentation: leasing can increase residency variance because hot pages get retained. Maybe evictor can prefer pages with zero leases and maintain a hotscore that decays faster for leased pages.

Devin: Another approach: ownership token + transfer API. When a page is handed off, producer calls `handoff(page, token)` and consumer claims `claim(token)`. Deterministic transfer but requires synchronous handoffs.

Liam: Sync handoff is simpler correctness-wise but will block producers, hurting throughput. Maybe allow both: sync handoff opt-in for hot pages, lease for everything else. We should expose an escape hatch for latency-sensitive paths to request synchronous claim with a short timeout.

Sophia: Implementation notes: use 64-bit token with epoch + counter to avoid ABA. Keep token table sharded per-NUMA for low contention. For cluster-global leases/tokens use a small consensus-free lease coordinator (leaderless with vector clocks) or piggyback on our existing placement service. Telemetry: token issuance rate, failed claims, avg claim latency, revoke counts, TTL expirations.

Maya: Agreed on hybrid model. Action items:
- Devin: prototype token claim/handoff (sync path) (due EOW)
- Sophia: prototype lease-based revocation + metrics (POC next week)
- Chris: add test cases for use-after-evict and cross-node claim races
- Liam: define rollout strategy and telemetry dashboards

OncallBot: Deploy scheduled: none. (no alerts)

Maya: Thanks all. We should sync in the design sync on Thursday 11am. :thumbsup:
